facts.label: Histórias no passado
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para a ação longa e o passado simples para o momento: I was baking a pie when you called.

facts.label: Ação em andamento
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para uma ação que estava acontecendo: I was baking a pie. You were playing on the porch. Use was com I, he, she e it. Use were com you, we e they.

facts.label: Quando
facts.sub: Use when + passado simples para o momento que interrompe: I was baking when you called. Marco was playing when I took the pie out. A ação curta usa o passado simples.

compare.us: Em inglês: I was baking when you called. Use was/were + -ing e when + passado simples.

answers: We say “I was baking” for an action in the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I was bake”. → Falso (We say I was baking.)
“When you called” gives the moment. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A cozy house · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday afternoon in a cozy house in Calgary. The oven is warm and the kitchen smells sweet. Gwen wipes her hands on a blue apron. Her grandson Marco comes in from the porch. There is a pie on the table. Gwen tells him a story.

“Marco, welcome! I was baking a pie when you called.” says Gwen. “It smells great, Gwen. When I was a boy, I always ate your pie.” says Marco. “Yes! You were playing on the porch when I took it out of the oven.” says Gwen.
